react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA (merged KEGG+WikiPathways+Reactome) returned KEGG:map00380 as its top hit with an FDR of 8.6e-19 and 7 of 54 pathway metabolites detected (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, serotonin, L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, melatonin). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returned KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with p=5.41e-09, overlapping the same 6 core metabolites across a 41-member KEGG pathway roster. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 with p=0.00126 and near-complete pathway coverage (16 of 17 empirical-compound network members). Secondary RaMP hits included serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR=2.1e-08), the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR=9.5e-09), and NAD+ biosynthetic pathways (WP:WP3645, FDR=2.1e-08), all consistent with tryptophan as the central substrate. L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the sole driver metabolite present in all four top-ranked hits across all three paradigms. Serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598) are co-detected in three of the four consensus pathways, consistent with bidirectional flux through the serotonin-melatonin branch. Quinolinic acid (C03722) anchors the kynurenine-to-NAD+ arm and appears in two pathways including NAD+ biosynthesis. The 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 hit (C19586) likely reflects xenobiotic stress co-occurring with, but peripheral to, the core tryptophan signal. Deoxyribose 1-phosphate and dihydrolipoate map to the pentose phosphate pathway and ascorbate metabolism respectively, consistent with secondary oxidative-stress co-variance.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as its top hit with FDR 8.59e-19 and 7 of 54 pathway metabolites detected, including L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returned KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with p=5.41e-09 and 6 of 41 pathway members, overlapping 6 of the same core metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 with p=0.00143 and 16 of 17 empirical-compound network members, providing near-complete pathway coverage. Secondary RaMP hits include the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 9.48e-09) and tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR 9.41e-11). Reactome Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.14e-08) and NAD+ biosynthetic pathways (WP:WP3645, FDR 2.14e-08) further validate the core signal. L-Tryptophan is the sole driver metabolite present in all four top-ranked hits across all three paradigms, consistent with it serving as the central substrate for downstream serotonin-melatonin and kynurenine-NAD+ branch points. Serotonin and melatonin co-detection is consistent with bidirectional flux through the serotonin-melatonin branch. Quinolinic acid anchors the kynurenine-to-NAD+ arm of tryptophan catabolism. 2,3-Epoxyaflatoxin B1 does not map to the top hits and likely reflects xenobiotic stress co-occurring with the core tryptophan signal.

RaMP multi-database ORA (merged KEGG+WikiPathways+Reactome) returned KEGG:map00380 as its top hit with an FDR of 8.6e-19 and 7 of 54 pathway metabolites detected (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, serotonin, L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, melatonin). final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this dataset. RaMP multi-database ORA (merged KEGG+WikiPathways+Reactome) returned KEGG:map00380 as its top hit with an FDR of 8.6e-19 and 7 of 54 pathway metabolites detected (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, serotonin, L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, melatonin). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returned KEGG:hsa00380 at rank 0 with p=5.41e-09, overlapping the same 6 core metabolites across a 41-member KEGG pathway roster. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 with p=0.00126 and near-complete pathway coverage (16 of 17 empirical-compound network members). Secondary RaMP hits included serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR=2.1e-08), the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR=9.5e-09), and NAD+ biosynthetic pathways (WP:WP3645, FDR=2.1e-08), all consistent with tryptophan as the central substrate. L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the sole driver metabolite present in all four top-ranked hits across all three paradigms. Serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598) are co-detected in three of the four consensus pathways, consistent with bidirectional flux through the serotonin-melatonin branch. Quinolinic acid (C03722) anchors the kynurenine-to-NAD+ arm and appears in two pathways including NAD+ biosynthesis. The 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 hit (C19586) likely reflects xenobiotic stress co-occurring with, but peripheral to, the core tryptophan signal. Deoxyribose 1-phosphate and dihydrolipoate map to the pentose phosphate pathway and ascorbate metabolism respectively, consistent with secondary oxidative-stress co-variance.
